title: Peter's first sermon (Acts 2:14–36)
hookLine: the denier stands up and preaches, quoting Joel and the Psalms
tomorrow: the crowd asks 'what shall we do?' so what did they actually do?

lines: I DO NOT KNOW THE MAN.
cards: After a public mistake, the hardest moment is often the next time you have to speak. Not long ago on this path, Peter stood by a fire in a courtyard and said, "I do not know the man."
Now, with a crowd from every nation watching, "Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice." He doesn't open with an apology.
He answers the mockers, then reaches for a prophet: "But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel."

teach.b: Today's question: who does God speak through?
Peter's answer is Joel's: "I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams."
Then, "on my servants and on my handmaidens." Listen to that list. Daughters.
Servants. The old and the young. Not only leaders, and not only people with a clean record; the man reading it aloud is proof of that.
Peter goes on to a psalm of David and to what he has seen: "This Jesus hath God raised up, whereof we all are witnesses."

teach.h: UNTO YOU, AND TO YOUR CHILDREN.
teach.b: And where the sermon lands, the promise widens again: "For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off." Now something Christians share with a neighbor. Joel's words aren't only in Acts.

teach.h: JOEL, IN THE JEWISH BIBLE TOO.
teach.b: They stand in the Jewish Bible, in the book of Joel, where the 1917 Jewish Publication Society translation reads, "I will pour out My spirit upon all flesh."
The same promise, all flesh, sons and daughters, old and young, stands in both Bibles. And one honest difference: Peter reads Joel as coming true that morning, through Jesus.
Jewish tradition reads Joel within Israel's own story, and not through Peter's reading of Jesus. One set of words, held by two peoples, read two ways.
One to tell a friend: Joel says afterward; Peter says in the last days.

how: Some churches read Peter's Pentecost sermon (Acts 2) on Pentecost Sunday; Joel's words about the Spirit poured on all flesh are also read in some churches on that day.

s: Peter apologizes for his denial before he preaches
he answers the mockers and reaches for Joel. Acts 2 doesn't mention the courtyard.
Joel's promise names daughters and handmaidens, not only sons
your sons and your daughters shall prophesy… on my servants and on my handmaidens.
Joel's words appear only in the Christian Bible
they're in the book of Joel in the Jewish Bible too: I will pour out My spirit upon all flesh.

games.q: a coworker blew a big presentation last month. the boss asks who'll present the next one, and she quietly raises her hand. people glance around. what fits Peter's sermon?
o: back her: one failure doesn't cancel her voice.
suggest someone with a clean record this time.
let her, once she apologizes to the team first.
games.why: the man who denied Jesus stood up with the eleven and lifted up his voice. Acts doesn't make him earn it back with a speech about the past.

practice: Write by hand the first sentence you'd say if you had to speak again after a stumble: to a friend, a class, a team. Keep it short and true, with no apology speech attached.
If you pray, you can offer it up; if not, read it once, slowly, and let it stand.

wordCard.voice: Peter's first sermon. The man who denied Jesus stands up, reads Joel's promise to all flesh, and tells what he has seen.
